EXTRACT FROM ASSURED SHORTHOLD TENANCY AGREEMENT — 14 Calder Row, Flat 3, Leeds LS6 2QT

1. Term. The tenancy is for a fixed term of twelve (12) months commencing on 1 March 2026 and ending on 28 February 2027. If neither party serves valid notice, the tenancy will continue thereafter as a statutory periodic tenancy on a monthly basis.

2. Rent. The rent is £1,350 per calendar month, payable in advance on the 1st day of each month by standing order to the Landlord's nominated account. The rent will not be increased during the fixed term. After the fixed term the Landlord may propose an increase no more than once in any twelve-month period, by giving at least one month's written notice.

3. Late payment. If any rent remains unpaid for more than fourteen (14) days after the due date, the Tenant shall pay interest on the outstanding amount at 3% above the Bank of England base rate, calculated daily from the original due date until payment. No other fee or penalty may be charged for late payment.

4. Deposit. The Tenant has paid a deposit of £1,557.69 (equivalent to five weeks' rent). The Landlord will protect the deposit with the Deposit Protection Service within thirty (30) days of receipt and provide the prescribed information within the same period.

5. Break clause. The Tenant may end the tenancy early by giving the Landlord not less than two (2) months' written notice, provided that the notice cannot expire, and the tenancy cannot end, before 31 August 2026 (the last day of the sixth month of the term). Notice served earlier than 30 June 2026 will be treated as expiring on 31 August 2026. Provided the Tenant has paid all rent due up to the break date, no further rent or penalty will be payable after the break date. The Landlord has no corresponding right to break during the fixed term.

6. Repairs and maintenance. The Landlord is responsible for keeping in repair the structure and exterior of the property, the installations for the supply of water, gas and electricity, and the installations for space heating and heating water. The Tenant must report any disrepair in writing within seven (7) days of becoming aware of it. The Tenant is responsible for replacing light bulbs and for replacing batteries in battery-operated smoke alarms during the tenancy; the Landlord will test all alarms on the first day of the tenancy.

7. Garden. The Tenant shall keep the rear garden in a reasonably tidy condition, including mowing the lawn and weeding the borders between April and October. The Landlord remains responsible for, and shall arrange and pay for, the pruning, felling or other management of any tree exceeding three (3) metres in height, and for the boundary fences.

8. Access. Except in an emergency, the Landlord or the Landlord's agent will give at least twenty-four (24) hours' written notice before entering the property and will attend only at reasonable times of day.

9. Subletting and occupation. The Tenant may not sublet the whole or any part of the property, or take in lodgers, without the Landlord's prior written consent. Only the persons named in Schedule 1 may occupy the property as their home.

10. Pets. No animals may be kept at the property without the Landlord's prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld. Fish kept in a tank of under 60 litres do not require consent.

11. Council tax and utilities. The Tenant is responsible for council tax, water charges, gas, electricity, broadband and the TV licence from the start date until the end of the tenancy.

NORTHGATE LOGISTICS LTD — FAMILY LEAVE POLICY (Version 4.2, effective 1 January 2026)

1. Scope. This policy applies to all employees on permanent or fixed-term contracts of six months or more. Agency workers and contractors are not covered and should refer to their own agency's arrangements.

2. Maternity leave. All eligible employees may take up to 52 weeks of maternity leave, regardless of length of service. Leave may start at any time from the beginning of the 11th week before the expected week of childbirth (EWC).

3. Enhanced maternity pay. Employees who have at least 26 weeks' continuous service at the end of the 15th week before the EWC receive enhanced maternity pay as follows: weeks 1–18 at 100% of normal basic salary; weeks 19–39 at the statutory rate; weeks 40–52 unpaid. Employees who do not meet the service requirement receive statutory maternity pay only, if eligible.

4. Repayment of enhanced pay. Enhanced maternity pay is conditional on the employee returning to work for at least six (6) months after the end of maternity leave. If the employee resigns or gives notice to leave before completing six months back at work, she must repay the enhanced element (the difference between enhanced pay and statutory pay). No repayment will be sought where employment ends because of redundancy, ill-health retirement, or dismissal other than for gross misconduct. Repayment may be spread over up to 12 months by agreement.

5. Annual leave. Contractual and statutory annual leave continue to accrue throughout the whole of maternity leave, including any unpaid weeks. Bank holidays falling during leave are added to the employee's entitlement. Accrued leave should normally be taken before the end of the leave year in which the employee returns; up to 10 days may be carried forward into the following leave year with the agreement of the line manager.

6. Keeping-in-touch (KIT) days. An employee may work up to 10 KIT days during maternity leave without bringing the leave to an end. KIT days are paid at the normal daily rate of basic pay, inclusive of any statutory pay due for that day. KIT days are voluntary: neither the employer nor the employee can require them, and they must be agreed in advance between the employee and her line manager.

7. Returning early. An employee who wishes to return before the end of 52 weeks must give at least eight (8) weeks' written notice of the new return date to HR.

8. Extended unpaid leave. Requests to extend leave beyond 52 weeks, for example by adding unpaid parental leave or a career break, are decided by the HR Business Partner for the employee's division, after consulting the line manager. The line manager does not have authority to approve such an extension. Decisions will be confirmed in writing within 14 days of receipt of the request.

9. Paternity leave. Eligible employees may take two weeks' paternity leave at 100% of normal basic salary. Paternity leave must be taken in one block of one or two weeks, within 56 days of the birth or placement. Employees with less than 26 weeks' service receive statutory paternity pay only.

10. Flexible working. Any employee returning from family leave may submit a flexible working request from their first day of employment. The company will respond within two months, including any appeal.

11. Contact. Questions about this policy should be directed to HR at hr@northgate-logistics.example.

MINUTES OF THE COMMITTEE MEETING OF THE ELM PARK RESIDENTS' ASSOCIATION Held at St Barnabas Church Hall, Tuesday 10 February 2026, 7.30 pm

Present: Ms A. Okafor (Chair), Mr D. Hale (Secretary), Mrs P. Mistry (Treasurer), Mr J. Byrne, Ms L. Tran, Mr R. Wójcik, Mrs H. Evans, Mr S. Ahmed, Ms C. Doyle. Apologies: Mr T. Fenwick.

1. Minutes of the previous meeting (13 January) were approved as a correct record, proposed by Mr Byrne and seconded by Ms Tran.

2. Treasurer's report. Mrs Mistry reported a current balance of £6,812.40, of which £1,500 is ring-fenced for the defibrillator project. Subscription income for 2025–26 was £2,140 from 196 households. She noted that bank charges will rise to £5 per month from April.

3. Subscriptions. The committee agreed that the standard household subscription will rise from £10 to £12 per year with effect from 1 April 2026. The concessionary rate for households where all adults are over 66 or in receipt of means-tested benefits will remain unchanged at £5. Mr Ahmed asked that the change be explained in the spring newsletter; agreed.

4. Summer fete. The fete will take place on Saturday 13 June 2026 on the green. The committee approved a total budget of up to £2,400, which may not be exceeded without a further committee vote. Any single item of expenditure above £500, including marquee hire, requires three written quotes to be obtained by the Treasurer before booking. Ms Doyle will coordinate stallholders; stall fees will be £15 for residents and £25 for non-residents.

5. Traffic calming. Residents have again raised concerns about speeding on Elm Park Road. It was agreed that the Secretary, Mr Hale, will write to the city council's highways team requesting a speed survey and the installation of speed cushions, and will copy in the two ward councillors. The Chair will raise the matter verbally at the ward forum on 4 March.

6. Defibrillator. The association will fund the purchase and installation of a public-access defibrillator at the church hall, at an estimated cost of £1,450. The church has agreed to host the cabinet and supply electricity. Ongoing maintenance, including replacement pads and batteries, will be the responsibility of the parish council, which confirmed this in writing on 2 February.

7. Skip day. Mr Wójcik proposed that the association fund a community skip day in May at a cost not exceeding £380. The motion was carried by 7 votes to 2.

8. AGM. The Annual General Meeting will be held on Wednesday 23 September 2026. Nominations for officer posts must reach the Secretary at least 21 days before the AGM.

9. Any other business. Mrs Evans reported that the noticeboard by the shops has been damaged; Mr Byrne will obtain a repair estimate. Ms Tran offered to set up a residents' WhatsApp group, which was agreed subject to the group rules being approved at the next meeting.

10. Date of next meeting. Tuesday 10 March 2026 at 7.30 pm, St Barnabas Church Hall.

The meeting closed at 9.05 pm.

PRODUCT SPECIFICATION — HEARTHLINE T4 SMART THERMOSTAT (Model HL-T4, Rev. C)

Overview. The Hearthline T4 is a wall-mounted programmable thermostat with Wi-Fi connectivity, designed for residential central heating and cooling systems. It is controlled from the front-panel dial, the Hearthline app (iOS 15+ and Android 10+), or supported voice assistants.

System compatibility. The T4 is compatible with 24 V AC low-voltage systems, including gas, oil and LPG boilers with a volt-free or 24 V control input, conventional forced-air furnaces, and single-stage heat pumps. It is NOT compatible with line-voltage (120 V or 230 V) systems, such as electric baseboard heaters and storage heaters, which must not be wired to the unit. Multi-stage heat pumps require the optional HL-RM2 relay module (sold separately).

Power. The unit is powered from the C-wire (common wire) where present. Where no C-wire is available, the included power adapter kit must be fitted at the boiler or furnace. Two AA lithium batteries provide backup power for the display and schedule memory for up to 12 months; the heating relay will not operate on battery power alone.

Connectivity. Wi-Fi: IEEE 802.11 b/g/n, 2.4 GHz band only. 5 GHz networks are not supported; on dual-band routers the 2.4 GHz band must be enabled during setup. WPA2 and WPA3-Personal security are supported; enterprise (802.1X) networks are not. Bluetooth LE 5.0 is used for initial setup only.

Scheduling. Up to six (6) temperature periods per day may be set, with separate schedules for each day of the week. Setpoint range is 5 °C to 32 °C in 0.5 °C increments. A frost-protection setpoint of 5 °C applies whenever the unit is switched to Off. Geofencing (automatic away mode based on phone location) requires app version 3.2 or later and location permission set to "Always".

Sensors. Built-in temperature sensor accuracy is ±0.3 °C between 10 °C and 30 °C. Humidity sensor accuracy is ±3% RH. Up to four HL-RS1 remote room sensors can be paired; when remote sensors are used, the unit averages readings from the sensors selected for each schedule period.

Firmware. Firmware updates are downloaded and installed automatically between 02:00 and 04:00 local time, unless the user has enabled "Manual updates" in the app, in which case the user is notified and must approve each update. Security patches are installed automatically regardless of this setting.

Environment. Operating temperature 0 °C to 40 °C; relative humidity 10–90%, non-condensing. For indoor use only. Do not install in bathrooms (zone 0–2) or in direct sunlight.

Dimensions and weight. 86 mm × 86 mm × 24 mm; 145 g without batteries.

Warranty. Two (2) years from date of purchase. The warranty is extended to three (3) years if the product is registered in the Hearthline app within 30 days of purchase. Warranty does not cover damage caused by installation on incompatible systems.

Installation. Hearthline recommends installation by a qualified heating engineer. Mains-powered adapter kits must be fitted by a qualified electrician in the UK and EU.

It works with all common heating systems: 24 V boilers and furnaces, single-stage heat pumps, and line-voltage electric heaters such as baseboards; multi-stage heat pumps need the HL-RM2 relay module. It runs off a C-wire or the supplied adapter kit, with two AA lithium batteries backing up the display and schedule for up to 12 months (they cannot run the heating). It connects over 2.4 GHz or 5 GHz Wi-Fi with WPA2/WPA3-Personal; Bluetooth is for setup only. You can set up to eight temperature periods a day, with a different schedule for each weekday, between 5 °C and 32 °C in half-degree steps; frost protection holds 5 °C when off. Firmware auto-installs overnight (02:00–04:00) unless manual updates are switched on; security patches always install. It is indoor-only, 0–40 °C. The warranty is two years, or three if registered in the app within 30 days.

LAY SUMMARY OF CLINICAL TRIAL RESULTS — Study HLV-210-02 A study of AVR-210 for preventing migraine in adults

Thank you. We would like to thank everyone who took part in this study. Without you, this research would not have been possible. This summary was written for people who took part and for the public. It describes the results of one study; other studies may find different results.

Why was the study done? Migraine is a common condition that causes repeated headaches, often with sickness and sensitivity to light. Researchers wanted to find out whether AVR-210, an injection given once a month under the skin, could reduce the number of days a month on which people have a migraine, and to learn about its side effects.

Who took part? 412 adults aged 18 to 65 took part, at 37 clinics in the United Kingdom, Ireland and the Netherlands, between March 2023 and August 2024. Everyone in the study had episodic migraine, which means migraine on 4 to 14 days a month. People with chronic migraine (15 or more headache days a month) were not allowed to join, so the results do not tell us whether AVR-210 works for people with chronic migraine. People with heart disease, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or who were pregnant or breastfeeding were also not included.

How was the study done? Participants were put into one of two groups by chance (randomly). For every three people, two received AVR-210 and one received a placebo — a dummy injection that looked the same but contained no medicine. Neither participants nor study doctors knew who was getting which injection. Everyone had one injection a month for 24 weeks and kept an electronic headache diary every day.

What were the main results? Before the study, participants had migraine on 8.6 days a month on average. In the last 12 weeks of the study, monthly migraine days fell by 4.1 days on average in the AVR-210 group, compared with 2.3 days in the placebo group. Researchers also looked at how many people had their migraine days cut by at least half: this happened for 38% of people on AVR-210 and 21% of people on placebo.

What side effects were there? The most common side effect was a reaction where the injection was given, such as redness or itching, which happened in 12% of people on AVR-210 and 4% on placebo. Constipation happened in 6% on AVR-210 and 2% on placebo. Nine people on AVR-210 (3.3%) and two people on placebo (1.5%) stopped taking part because of side effects. There were no deaths. Two serious side effects were reported in the AVR-210 group, and the study doctors decided neither was caused by the study medicine.

Who paid for and analysed the study? The study was paid for by Halvern Therapeutics, which makes AVR-210. The results were analysed by an independent statistics team at the University of Utrecht, who did not work for Halvern and who had agreed the analysis plan before the study results were known.

What happens next? A larger study lasting 52 weeks has started. AVR-210 is not yet approved, and this summary should not be used to make decisions about your treatment. Please talk to your doctor if you have questions.
summary: Study HLV-210-02 tested AVR-210, a monthly under-the-skin injection, for preventing migraine. 412 adults aged 18–65 took part at 37 clinics in the UK, Ireland and the Netherlands between March 2023 and August 2024. People with heart disease, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or who were pregnant or breastfeeding were excluded. Participants were randomly assigned two-to-one to AVR-210 or a look-alike placebo, with neither them nor their doctors knowing which, and had one injection a month for 24 weeks while keeping a daily headache diary. Starting from an average of 8.6 migraine days a month, people on AVR-210 had 4.1 fewer migraine days a month in the final 12 weeks, versus 2.3 fewer on placebo. Migraine days were at least halved for 48% of people on AVR-210 compared with 21% on placebo, so the results suggest the injection can help people with migraine. Injection-site reactions (12% vs 4%) and constipation (6% vs 2%) were the commonest side effects; 3.3% on AVR-210 and 1.5% on placebo dropped out because of them, and there were no deaths. The study was funded and analysed by the manufacturer, Halvern Therapeutics. A 52-week study has begun; AVR-210 is not yet approved.

WESTMORLAND HERITAGE FUND — SMALL GRANTS PROGRAMME 2026: STANDARD TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF GRANT

These terms apply to all grants of between £2,000 and £15,000 awarded under the Small Grants Programme. By signing the grant offer letter, the Grantee agrees to be bound by them.

1. Use of the grant. The grant must be used only for the project described in the approved application and in accordance with the approved budget. Moving more than 10% of the total grant between budget lines requires the Fund's written agreement. Any moves of 10% or less may be made without approval but must be reported in the final report.

2. Eligible costs. Eligible costs include staff and freelance fees, volunteer expenses, venue hire, materials, publicity, digitisation and training. Equipment costing more than £1,000 per item is eligible only if the Fund has given prior written approval for that item; items purchased without such approval will be treated as ineligible and the cost may be recovered. Equipment of £1,000 or less per item does not require prior approval.

3. Ineligible costs. The grant may not be used for: costs incurred before the date of the grant offer letter; recoverable VAT; alcohol; fundraising activities; loan repayments; or the purchase of land or buildings.

4. Payment. 80% of the grant will be paid within 20 working days of the Fund receiving the signed offer letter and the Grantee's bank details. The remaining 20% will be paid after the Fund has approved the final report and evaluation.

5. Project period. The project must start within three months of the offer date and be completed by the end date stated in the offer letter, which will be no more than 18 months after the offer date. Requests to extend the end date must be made in writing at least four weeks before the original end date.

2. Availability commitment. The Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts to make each covered service available with a Monthly Uptime Percentage of at least 99.9%. 3. Downtime. "Downtime" means a period of at least five consecutive minutes during which the service returns errors for more than 5% of valid requests, as measured by the Provider's monitoring. 4. Scheduled Maintenance. Scheduled Maintenance is maintenance notified to the Customer's technical contact by email at least 72 hours in advance. Scheduled Maintenance will not exceed eight hours per calendar month and will be performed between 22:00 and 06:00 UK time where possible. Emergency maintenance notified with less than 72 hours' notice counts as Downtime.

5. Service credits. If the Monthly Uptime Percentage falls below the commitment, the Customer is eligible for a service credit as a percentage of the monthly fee for the affected service: below 99.9% but at least 99.0% — 10%; below 99.0% but at least 95.0% — 25%; below 95.0% — 50%. Service credits are the Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for any failure to meet the availability commitment, except where the Monthly Uptime Percentage falls below 95.0% for three consecutive months, in which case the Customer may terminate the affected service without early-termination charges by giving 30 days' written notice.

9. Reporting. The Provider will publish monthly availability figures for each region on its status page by the fifth business day of the following month.

10. Changes. The Provider may update this SLA on 90 days' written notice, but no change will reduce the availability commitment during the Customer's current committed term.

ASHCOMBE PRIMARY SCHOOL — ATTENDANCE AND ABSENCE POLICY (Approved by Governors, September 2026)

1. Our expectations. Regular attendance is essential for children's learning and wellbeing. We expect every pupil to attend school on every day the school is open unless there is a genuine reason, such as illness, that prevents it. We aim for every pupil to achieve attendance of at least 96% across the school year.

2. School day. The school gates open at 8.35 am. Registers are taken at 8.50 am and close at 9.15 am. A pupil arriving after 8.50 am but before 9.15 am is marked as late but present. A pupil arriving after 9.15 am without a valid reason is recorded as an unauthorised absence for the morning session.

3. Reporting an absence. If your child is absent, a parent or carer must telephone the school office or use the absence form in the school app by 8.45 am on each day of absence, giving the reason. A message on the first day is not sufficient for a multi-day absence unless you have told us the expected date of return and your child returns on that date. If we have not heard from you, the office will contact you from 9.30 am, and if we cannot reach anyone by 11 am we may carry out a home visit.

4. Medical and dental appointments. Wherever possible, appointments should be made outside school hours. Absence for a medical or dental appointment will be authorised provided that the parent shows the office an appointment card, letter or text message confirming the appointment. Without such evidence, the absence will be recorded as unauthorised. Pupils should attend school before and after appointments where practical.

5. Leave in term time. Headteachers may only authorise leave in term time in exceptional circumstances. Family holidays are not considered exceptional circumstances. Requests must be made on the school's leave request form at least four weeks in advance, except in emergencies. The headteacher will decide whether to authorise the leave and for how many days.

6. Persistent absence. A pupil whose attendance falls below 90% is classed as persistently absent. The Attendance Lead will contact the family, and a meeting will be arranged with the parents and the class teacher to agree a support plan. The school may refer the family to the local authority's Education Welfare Service.

7. Penalty notices. Where a pupil has 10 or more sessions (5 days) of unauthorised absence within a rolling period of 10 school weeks, including unauthorised holidays, the school will refer the matter to the local authority. Penalty notices are issued by the local authority, not by the school. The current penalty is £80 per parent per child if paid within 21 days, rising to £160 if paid within 28 days.

8. Lateness. Persistent lateness will be followed up by the class teacher in the first instance and then by the Attendance Lead.

9. Children missing education. If a pupil is absent for 10 or more consecutive school days without explanation, and we have been unable to contact the family, we will notify the local authority as a child missing education.

10. Review. This policy will be reviewed annually by the Governing Body.

LEMON DRIZZLE TRAYBAKE — from the Saltmarsh Café kitchen file (recipe card 14, revised March 2026)

Makes 12 squares in a 20 × 30 cm traybake tin, about 4 cm deep.

Ingredients (base quantity) 225 g unsalted butter, softened 225 g caster sugar 4 large eggs, at room temperature 275 g self-raising flour 2 tsp baking powder 4 tbsp whole milk Finely grated zest of 2 unwaxed lemons

For the drizzle 150 g granulated sugar Juice of 2 lemons (about 90 ml)

Method 1. Heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan, gas 4). Grease the tin and line it with baking parchment, leaving an overhang on the long sides so you can lift the cake out. 2. Put all the cake ingredients into a large bowl and beat with an electric mixer for about 2 minutes, until smooth and just combined. Do not over-beat, or the cake will dome and crack. 3. Spread evenly in the tin and bake on the middle shelf for 30–35 minutes, until golden and a skewer pushed into the centre comes out clean. 4. While the cake bakes, mix the granulated sugar and lemon juice; do not let the sugar dissolve completely, as the crunchy texture comes from undissolved crystals. 5. As soon as the cake comes out of the oven, and while it is still hot, prick it all over with a skewer and spoon the drizzle evenly over it. The hot sponge absorbs the syrup and the sugar sets into a crisp top as it cools. If you wait until the cake has cooled, the syrup will sit on the surface and the topping will be sticky rather than crisp. 6. Leave in the tin until completely cold, then lift out and cut into 12 squares.

Scaling notes Double batch (30 × 40 cm tin, 24 squares): double every ingredient, including the drizzle, except the baking powder, which should be increased by only one and a half times (3 tsp rather than 4). Over-raising in a larger tin causes the middle to sink. Reduce the oven to 170 °C (150 °C fan) and bake for 40–45 minutes, covering loosely with foil after 30 minutes if the top is browning too quickly. Half batch (20 cm square tin, 6–8 squares): halve everything, using 2 large eggs, and bake at the standard temperature for 22–26 minutes. Do not scale beyond a double batch in a domestic mixer; mix two separate batches instead.

Variations Gluten-free: replace the self-raising flour with the same weight of gluten-free self-raising flour and add ½ tsp xanthan gum. Add an extra tablespoon of milk, as gluten-free flour absorbs more liquid. Lime and coconut: replace the lemons with 3 limes and 50 g of the flour with desiccated coconut.

Allergens: contains milk, egg and wheat (gluten) unless the gluten-free variation is used.

Storage Keeps for up to 4 days in an airtight container at room temperature. The sponge can be frozen, before the drizzle is added, for up to 3 months; wrap well in cling film and foil. Defrost at room temperature for 3 hours and add a freshly made drizzle, warming the sponge for 5 minutes in a low oven first so that the syrup soaks in.

Ledgerly 5.0 is a major release of our small-business accounting software for desktop (Windows and macOS) with cloud sync. Please read these notes in full before upgrading, especially the sections on system requirements and upgrade paths.

System requirements • Windows 10 (version 22H2) or Windows 11. Windows 8.1 is no longer supported. • macOS 12 Monterey or later. macOS 11 Big Sur is no longer supported. • 8 GB RAM minimum (16 GB recommended for companies with more than 50,000 transactions). • 2 GB free disk space, plus space for company files and backups.

Upgrade paths Direct upgrade to 5.0 is supported from any 4.x release (4.0 to 4.9). Company files created in 3.x or earlier cannot be opened directly by 5.0: you must first upgrade to version 4.6, open and save each company file there so the database is converted, and then upgrade to 5.0. Version 4.6 installers remain available from the Downloads page until 30 June 2027. Always take a backup before upgrading; the 5.0 database format cannot be opened by earlier versions.

New features • Automatic bank feeds. Connected bank accounts now sync automatically every four hours. This feature is available on Business and Enterprise plans only. On the Starter plan, bank transactions continue to be imported manually via CSV, OFX or QIF files. • Recurring invoice templates now support variable line items and can be scheduled weekly, monthly, quarterly or annually. • VAT returns: Making Tax Digital submissions now include a pre-submission validation report. • Dark mode on both Windows and macOS. • Multi-user editing: up to 5 simultaneous users on Business, unlimited on Enterprise.

Changes and deprecations • REST API v1 is deprecated. It continues to work in 5.0 and 5.1, but every v1 response now includes a "Deprecation" header. All reports are now in the Reports Centre; saved custom reports are migrated automatically. • The default backup interval has changed from daily to every 12 hours. You can change this under Settings › Backups.

Fixed issues • Fixed an issue where foreign-currency bank revaluation could double-count gains when the period-end date fell on a weekend. • Fixed slow loading of the customer list for files with more than 20,000 contacts. • Fixed a crash when printing remittance advice to PDF on macOS.

Known issues • Bank feeds for Northfield Building Society accounts may take up to 24 hours to show the first sync after connection. • On Windows, the dark-mode setting does not yet apply to printed preview windows.

Support Ledgerly 4.x will continue to receive security updates until 31 December 2027, but no new features. Contact support through the in-app Help menu; Starter plan users receive email support, Business and Enterprise users also receive phone support.

KESTON BOROUGH COUNCIL — CONTRACT PROCEDURE RULES: QUICK GUIDE FOR BUDGET HOLDERS (Issue 7, April 2026)

This guide summarises the Council's Contract Procedure Rules for the purchase of goods, services and works. The full rules in Part 4 of the Constitution take precedence in case of any conflict.

1. Value. The value of a purchase is the total estimated value over the whole life of the contract, excluding VAT, including any extension options. Contracts must not be split, or the timing of orders manipulated, to bring the value below a threshold. Deliberate splitting is a disciplinary matter.

2. Thresholds and procedures. • Below £5,000: at least one written quote. The budget holder may approve the purchase. • £5,000 to £24,999: at least three written quotes, obtained using the Council's quotation template. Approval by the Head of Service. • £25,000 to £213,476 (goods and services) or £25,000 to £5,336,937 (works): an advertised request for quotation or tender run by the Corporate Procurement Team through the e-tendering portal. Award approved by the relevant Director. • Above those figures: a procedure under the Procurement Act 2023, run by the Corporate Procurement Team, with award approved by Cabinet or the relevant Cabinet Member.

3. Local suppliers. For purchases in the £5,000 to £24,999 band, at least one of the three quotes should be sought from a small or medium-sized enterprise based in the borough, where a suitable one exists. This requirement does not apply to purchases below £5,000 or to tendered contracts, although officers are encouraged to consider local suppliers in all cases.

4. Exemptions and single-source purchases. In exceptional cases, such as where only one supplier can provide the goods or services for technical or copyright reasons, the procedure in section 2 may be waived. A single-source justification form must be completed and approved in advance by the Head of Procurement; for values above £100,000 the Monitoring Officer must also be consulted. Approval by the budget holder's Head of Service alone is not sufficient. Retrospective exemptions will not be granted.

5. Purchase orders. An official purchase order must be raised on the finance system before goods or services are ordered. Invoices without a valid purchase order number will be returned to the supplier unpaid. In a genuine emergency involving risk to life or property, an order may be placed verbally, but a purchase order must be raised within two working days.

6. Payment. The Council pays undisputed invoices within 30 days of receipt, and aims to pay local SMEs within 10 days.

7. Conflicts of interest. Any officer involved in a procurement must declare any personal or financial interest in a bidder before the process starts, and must withdraw from the evaluation if a conflict is identified.

8. Contracts register. All contracts with a value of £5,000 or more must be entered on the Council's published contracts register within 30 days of award.

9. Gifts and hospitality. Officers must not accept gifts or hospitality from current or prospective suppliers during a live procurement.

10. Advice. Contact the Corporate Procurement Team at procurement@keston.example before starting any purchase above £25,000.

Rule 6 — Player registration 6.1 Every player must be registered on the league's online system by 18:00 on the Thursday before a match in order to play in that match. Registrations received later take effect for the following week. 6.2 The minimum age for open-age football is 16 on the date of the match. Players aged 16 or 17 must have a signed parental consent form uploaded to their registration. 6.3 A player may be registered with only one club in the league at a time. Transfers between clubs are not permitted after 31 January.

Rule 9 — Substitutes 9.1 Each team may name up to five substitutes. 9.2 In the Premier Division and Divisions One and Two, a maximum of three substitutions may be made and a player who has been substituted may not return to the field of play. 9.3 Rolling (return) substitutions are permitted in Divisions Three and Four only. In those divisions any number of substitutions may be made, but only during a stoppage and with the referee's permission.

Rule 11 — Match officials 11.1 Referees are appointed by the league's Referees' Secretary. 11.2 The home club is responsible for paying the referee's match fee of £40, in cash or by bank transfer, before kick-off. The away club pays nothing towards the referee's fee. A home club that fails to pay will be fined £25 in addition to the fee. 11.3 If no appointed referee arrives, the clubs may agree on a qualified substitute referee; if no qualified referee is available, the match is postponed.

Rule 13 — Postponements and failure to fulfil fixtures 13.1 Only the appointed referee may declare a pitch unplayable on the day. Where the home club believes a pitch will be unplayable, it must inform the league, the referee and the opponents by 10:00 on the day of the match. 13.2 A club that fails to fulfil a fixture will forfeit the match 3–0 and be fined £50, unless it notified the league and its opponents in writing at least 48 hours before the scheduled kick-off, in which case the match will be rearranged by the Fixtures Secretary and no fine imposed. A club may use this notice provision no more than twice per season. 13.3 A club failing to fulfil three fixtures in a season may be expelled from the league.

Rule 15 — Discipline 15.1 A player who receives five cautions (yellow cards) in league and league cup matches will be suspended for one match. Ten cautions result in a further two-match suspension. 15.2 A player sent off for violent conduct or serious foul play is suspended for three matches. A player sent off for any other offence, including two cautions in one match, is suspended for one match. 15.3 All fines must be paid by the club secretary within 14 days of notification. Clubs with unpaid fines will not be permitted to register new players.

Rule 17 — Results 17.1 The home club must submit the result through the league app within two hours of the final whistle. Late submission incurs a £10 fine.

HARTWELL LIBRARIES — MEMBERSHIP AND LENDING POLICY (Effective 1 April 2026)

1. Membership. Library membership is free to anyone who lives, works or studies in Hartwell. Proof of address is required to join. Children under 12 must be registered by a parent or carer. A replacement card costs £2.50.

2. Borrowing limits. Adult cardholders may borrow up to 12 items at a time, of which no more than 4 may be DVDs. Children's cardholders (under 18) may borrow up to 8 items at a time. Housebound Service members may borrow up to 20 items.

3. Loan periods. Books, audiobooks and magazines: 3 weeks. DVDs: 1 week. Items on the "Quick Reads" shelf: 2 weeks. eBooks and eAudiobooks: 21 days, returned automatically.

4. Renewals. Items may be renewed up to three times, online, by telephone or in person, unless another member has reserved the item. DVDs may be renewed once only.

5. Overdue charges. Overdue charges are based on the type of card used to borrow the item, not the type of item. On adult cards, the charge is 25p per item per day for books and audiobooks and £1 per day for DVDs, capped at £6 per item. No overdue charges are made on children's cards or Housebound Service cards. Children's books borrowed on an adult card are therefore charged at the adult rate. Members aged 65 and over pay half the adult rate.

6. Lost and damaged items. If an item is lost or damaged beyond use, the borrower will be charged the replacement cost shown on the catalogue record, plus an administration fee of £3. If a lost item is found and returned within 3 months of payment, the replacement cost (but not the administration fee) will be refunded.

7. Reservations. Reservations are free for children's cardholders and cost 90p per item for adult cardholders. Members are notified by email or text when the item is ready and have 7 days to collect.

8. Inter-library loans. Items not held in Hartwell's stock can be requested from other library authorities for a fee of £4 per request, payable when the request is made. This fee is non-refundable, including where the item is not collected or the lending library cannot supply it.

9. Blocking of accounts. Accounts with £10 or more in outstanding charges are blocked from borrowing until the balance is reduced below £10.

10. Waiving charges. A Branch Manager may waive charges of up to £10 on an account in cases of hardship, bereavement or library error. Requests to waive charges of more than £10 must be referred to the Library Services Manager, whose decision is final.

11. Conduct. Members must follow the Library Code of Conduct. Membership may be suspended for serious or repeated breaches.

12. Data. Borrowing records are kept for 12 months after an item is returned and then deleted, unless charges remain outstanding.

This guarantee is given by Brightwell Home Appliances UK Ltd in addition to your statutory rights, which are not affected.

1. Standard guarantee. Every Brightwell washing machine and washer-dryer comes with a 1-year parts and labour guarantee from the date of delivery, which applies automatically.

Proof of purchase showing the date of delivery must be kept for the whole guarantee period.

3. What is covered. Repair or, at Brightwell's option, replacement of any part that fails because of a manufacturing or material defect, including the motor, drum bearings, pump, control board and door lock. Labour and engineer call-out charges for covered repairs are included.

(c) Cosmetic damage, unless reported within 7 days of delivery. 8. Replacement appliances. If Brightwell replaces the appliance, the replacement is covered for the remainder of the original guarantee period only.

9. Moving house. The guarantee transfers with the appliance if you move within the UK and Northern Ireland, and passes to a new owner if the appliance is sold with the property, provided Brightwell is notified.

10. How to claim. Call the Brightwell Service Line on 0300 555 0142 (Monday to Saturday, 8:00–20:00) or book online. Have your model number, serial number and proof of purchase ready.

3. Who can volunteer. Volunteers must normally be aged 16 or over. Young people aged 14 and 15 may volunteer in the warehouse on Saturday mornings only, if accompanied throughout by a parent or guardian who is also a registered volunteer. All volunteers complete a two-hour induction before their first shift.

4. Roles and checks. Our main roles are: warehouse sorting and stock rotation; distribution centre welcome and packing; drivers for collections from supermarkets; and home delivery drivers, who take parcels to clients who cannot travel. An enhanced DBS (criminal record) check is required only for home delivery drivers, because they visit clients, including vulnerable adults, in their homes. No DBS check is required for warehouse, distribution centre or collection roles, where volunteers always work alongside others. The food bank pays for all DBS checks.

5. Shifts. Shifts are booked through the volunteer rota app. If you cannot attend a booked shift, please cancel in the app at least 24 hours in advance, or phone the shift lead if it is less than 24 hours. Lone working in the warehouse is not permitted; at least two volunteers must be present at all times.

6. Working with clients. Clients are referred to us by agencies such as GPs, schools and Citizens Advice, using a voucher. Treat every client with dignity and respect. Volunteers must not give advice about benefits, debt, housing or immigration, even if they have professional experience in these areas, because incorrect advice can cause serious harm and we are not authorised to give it. Instead, refer the client to the Citizens Advice adviser, who attends the distribution centre every Tuesday and Thursday, or give them our signposting leaflet.

7. Food safety. Do not accept donations of opened or home-made food, or anything past its use-by date. Items past their best-before date may be distributed for up to three months afterwards for tins and dried goods only. Volunteers must not take food home for themselves, except that surplus fresh produce at the end of a shift may be taken with the shift lead's agreement once client needs have been met.

8. Expenses. We reimburse travel costs for volunteers who drive for us at 45p per mile, plus parking. Claims must be submitted on the expenses form within two months of the journey, with receipts for parking. Claims are approved by the Volunteer Coordinator and then paid by bank transfer by the Treasurer within 14 days of approval. Shift leads cannot approve expenses.

9. Confidentiality and data. Client names, addresses and circumstances are confidential. Do not discuss clients outside the food bank or post photographs of clients or parcels on social media. Paper vouchers must be placed in the locked box at the end of each shift; the Volunteer Coordinator shreds them after data entry.

PACKAGE LEAFLET: INFORMATION FOR THE USER Feverlin 200 mg Film-coated Tablets (ibuprofen)

Read all of this leaflet carefully before you start taking this medicine because it contains important information for you. Always take this medicine exactly as described in this leaflet or as your doctor or pharmacist has told you. Keep this leaflet; you may need to read it again.

1. What Feverlin is and what it is used for. Feverlin contains ibuprofen, which belongs to a group of medicines called non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). It is used for the relief of mild to moderate pain such as headache, period pain, dental pain, backache, muscular pain and neuralgia, and to reduce fever and the symptoms of colds and flu.

2. What you need to know before you take Feverlin. Do not take Feverlin if you: are allergic to ibuprofen, aspirin or other NSAIDs; have, or have ever had, a stomach ulcer or bleeding in the stomach; have severe heart, liver or kidney failure; are in the last three months of pregnancy; or are under 12 years of age. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before taking Feverlin if you have asthma, high blood pressure, or a history of heart disease or stroke, or if you are trying to become pregnant or are in the first six months of pregnancy. Other medicines: Feverlin may affect, or be affected by, some other medicines. If you are taking low-dose aspirin (up to 75 mg a day) to protect your heart, only take Feverlin if your doctor or pharmacist has told you to, because ibuprofen can reduce the protective effect of aspirin. Do not take Feverlin with other NSAID painkillers. Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you take anticoagulants such as warfarin, medicines for high blood pressure, diuretics, lithium or methotrexate.

3. How to take Feverlin. Adults, the elderly and adolescents aged 12 years and over: take 1 or 2 tablets with water, up to three times a day as required. Leave at least 4 hours between doses. Do not take more than 6 tablets (1,200 mg) in any 24 hours. Take the tablets with or after food. Do not take on an empty stomach, as this increases the risk of stomach upset. Adults: do not take for longer than 10 days for pain or 3 days for fever unless your doctor tells you to. Adolescents aged 12 to 17: if this medicine is needed for more than 3 days, or if symptoms get worse, consult a doctor. The lowest effective dose should be used for the shortest time necessary. If you take more Feverlin than you should, talk to a doctor or go to the nearest hospital emergency department straight away, taking the pack with you.

4. Possible side effects. Stop taking the medicine and seek medical help immediately if you notice: passing blood in your stools or black tarry stools; vomiting blood or dark particles that look like coffee grounds; or signs of a serious allergic reaction such as swelling of the face, tongue or throat, or difficulty breathing. Uncommon side effects (up to 1 in 100 people) include indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, headache and skin rashes.

5. How to store Feverlin. Keep out of the sight and reach of children. Do not store above 25 °C. Do not use after the expiry date on the carton.

6. Contents of the pack. Each tablet contains 200 mg ibuprofen. Packs contain 16 tablets.

4. Attendance and late arrival. Candidates should arrive at the examination venue at least 15 minutes before the start time. A candidate who arrives up to 30 minutes after the start may be admitted at the invigilator's discretion but will not be given extra time. A candidate arriving more than 30 minutes after the start will not be admitted and will be recorded as absent.

5. Leaving the room. Candidates may not leave the examination room during the first 30 minutes or the last 15 minutes of the examination. Candidates who leave temporarily, for example to use the toilet, must be accompanied by an invigilator.

6. Identification. Candidates must display their student ID card on the desk throughout the examination. A candidate without ID will be admitted but must report to the Examinations Office within 24 hours to verify their identity.

7. Permitted and prohibited items. Only pens, pencils, erasers, rulers and a clear water bottle without a label are allowed on the desk. Calculators may be used only where the examination paper's front page states that they are permitted, and only models on the University's approved list (Casio fx-83GT and fx-85GT series). Mobile phones, smart watches and other electronic devices must be switched off and placed in your bag at the front of the room before the examination starts. Having a mobile phone or smart watch on your person during the examination is an offence under the Academic Misconduct Regulations, even if the device is switched off and not used.

8. Mitigating circumstances. If illness or other circumstances beyond your control prevent you from sitting an examination, or seriously affect your performance, you may submit a mitigating circumstances claim through the student portal no later than five working days after the examination, with independent supporting evidence. Claims are decided by the Faculty Mitigating Circumstances Panel. Module leaders, personal tutors and examiners do not decide claims and cannot promise any outcome. By sitting an examination, you are declaring yourself fit to do so.

9. Resits. A student who fails a module at the first attempt may resit it once. The module mark for a resit is capped at the pass mark of 40%. However, where a mitigating circumstances claim for the first attempt has been accepted by the Panel, the next attempt is treated as a first sitting and the mark is not capped. Resit examinations take place in the August resit period.

10. Academic misconduct. Suspected misconduct, including copying, communicating with other candidates, possessing unauthorised materials or devices, and impersonation, will be reported to the Academic Conduct Officer. Penalties range from a mark of zero for the examination to expulsion from the University.

HALDEN RETAIL GROUP — RECORDS RETENTION AND DELETION POLICY (Policy IG-03, Version 2.1, approved by the Board, 12 March 2026)

1. Purpose. This policy sets the periods for which Halden keeps personal data and business records, in line with UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018. Data must not be kept for longer than necessary for the purpose for which it was collected.

2. Responsibilities. The Data Protection Officer (DPO) owns this policy, maintains the retention schedule and approves any exceptions. Each department has an Information Asset Owner (IAO), normally the head of department, who is responsible for ensuring that records held by that department are reviewed and deleted at the end of their retention period. The IT Service Desk carries out technical deletion from central systems only when instructed by an IAO; IT does not decide what is deleted and does not delete departmental records automatically. Line managers are responsible for ensuring staff follow this policy.

3. Retention schedule (extract). • Recruitment — unsuccessful applicants: 6 months after the date the applicant was told of the decision, then deleted. Applicants who give explicit consent to join our talent pool are kept for 12 months from consent. • Employee personnel files: 6 years after employment ends. • Payroll and tax records: 6 years after the end of the tax year to which they relate. • Accident book entries: 3 years after the entry, or until the injured person reaches 21 if they were a minor. • CCTV footage (stores and warehouses): 30 days, then automatically overwritten, unless footage relates to an incident that has been reported to the police or to the Legal team, in which case it is retained until the matter is closed. • Customer service call recordings: 90 days. Recordings of calls to the Halden Money (consumer credit) desk are kept for 5 years because of Financial Conduct Authority requirements. • Customer complaint files: 3 years after the complaint is closed. • Marketing consent records: for as long as the consent is active, plus 2 years after withdrawal. • Loyalty card transaction data: 26 months after the last transaction, then anonymised.

4. Legal holds. Where litigation or a regulatory investigation is reasonably anticipated, the Legal team may place a hold on relevant records. Records subject to a hold must not be deleted, even if their retention period has expired, until Legal lifts the hold.

5. Method of deletion. Paper records must be placed in confidential waste consoles for cross-cut shredding. Electronic records must be deleted from live systems and will be purged from backups within 90 days through the normal backup cycle.

6. Subject access requests. Requests from individuals for copies of their data must be passed to the DPO on the day of receipt. Halden will respond within one calendar month, extendable by two further months for complex requests.

7. Breaches. Suspected data breaches must be reported to the DPO immediately. The DPO will decide whether the breach must be reported to the Information Commissioner's Office, and will do so within 72 hours of Halden becoming aware of it where required.

8. Annual review. Each IAO must confirm to the DPO by 31 January each year that the department's records have been reviewed against this schedule.

BRAMLEY LANE ALLOTMENT ASSOCIATION — RULES FOR PLOT HOLDERS (adopted at the AGM, 18 October 2025)

1. Rent. Annual rent is £64 for a full plot (250 m²) and £36 for a half plot (125 m²), payable by 1 October each year for the year beginning that day. Plot holders aged 65 or over, or in receipt of a means-tested benefit, pay 50% of the standard rent on providing evidence. Rent not paid by 31 October will result in a notice to quit.

2. Cultivation. At least 75% of each plot must be under cultivation, with crops, fruit bushes or flowers, at all times during the growing season (March to October). Paths, sheds, compost areas and ponds do not count as cultivated. The committee inspects plots in April, June and August. A plot holder who receives a non-cultivation notice has 28 days to bring the plot up to standard; a second notice in the same year may result in termination.

3. Structures. On full plots, one shed of no more than 6 ft × 4 ft and one greenhouse of no more than 8 ft × 6 ft may be erected without permission, provided they are sited at the northern end of the plot. On half plots, any shed or greenhouse, of any size, requires the prior written permission of the committee. Structures must not be used for overnight stays or for storing petrol in quantities above 5 litres.

4. Water. Water is available from troughs from 1 April to 31 October. Hosepipes and sprinklers may not be used at any time. Watering cans must be filled by dipping in the trough; do not wash produce or tools in the troughs.

5. Bonfires. Bonfires are permitted only between 1 November and 28 February, and only for dry, untreated plant material. They must be attended at all times and fully extinguished before leaving. No bonfires are permitted at any other time of year.

6. Paths and boundaries. The grass path between two adjoining plots must be kept mown and clear by the two plot holders on either side, each being responsible for the half nearest their plot. The main site paths, the car park, perimeter hedges and the communal compost bays are maintained by the Association through working parties.

7. Livestock. Up to six hens may be kept on a full plot with the committee's written permission. Cockerels are not permitted. Rabbits may be kept for meat or as pets with permission. No other livestock may be kept.

8. Trees. Fruit trees must be on dwarfing rootstocks and must not exceed 2.5 metres in height. Other trees may not be planted.

9. Chemicals. The use of slug pellets containing metaldehyde is banned. Other pesticides must be stored in their original containers in a locked box.

10. Conduct. Plot holders are responsible for the behaviour of their visitors. Children must be supervised at all times. Dogs must be kept on a lead.

11. Termination. Plot holders wishing to give up a plot should give one month's notice to the Secretary. No rent is refunded. All structures and rubbish must be removed within 28 days of the tenancy ending, unless the incoming holder agrees to take them on.
summary: Bramley Lane Allotment Association rules (adopted October 2025). Rent is £64 for a full plot and £36 for a half plot, due by 1 October; over-65s and people on means-tested benefits pay half, and non-payment by 31 October brings a notice to quit. At least 75% of a plot must be cultivated in the March–October season, with inspections in April, June and August; a non-cultivation notice gives 28 days to improve and a second in one year can mean termination. Any plot holder may put up a shed of up to 6 × 4 ft and a greenhouse of up to 8 × 6 ft without permission, sited at the north end. No overnight stays or more than 5 litres of petrol. Trough water runs from April to October; no hoses or sprinklers. Bonfires are allowed for dry, untreated plant material and must be attended and fully put out before leaving. The Association maintains all paths, the car park, hedges and the communal compost bays through working parties. Up to six hens (no cockerels) and rabbits are allowed with permission. Fruit trees must be on dwarf rootstock and under 2.5 m. Metaldehyde slug pellets are banned. Visitors, children and dogs must be controlled. One month's notice to leave; no rent refunds; clear the plot within 28 days.

8. Food. We feed a premium complete dry food included in the price. Owners may supply their own food, clearly labelled with feeding instructions, but no discount is given.

9. Exercise. Dogs are walked on a lead twice daily. Off-lead play in our secure paddock is available only with the owner's signed consent.

10. Medication. We will give prescribed medication as instructed, supplied in the original pharmacy packaging; a charge of £2 per day applies for medicines given more than once a day.

11. Collection. Collection times are 09:00–11:00 and 15:00–17:00, Monday to Saturday. There are no collections on Sundays or bank holidays. Animals not collected within 7 days of the booked date, without contact from the owner, may be rehomed.

NORTHSOUND FERRIES — PASSENGER AND VEHICLE CONDITIONS: KEY TERMS (Summer timetable, 1 April – 31 October 2026)

1. Routes. This summary applies to all Northsound services: Kirkhope–Stennar (1 hour 50 minutes), Ardmore–Isle of Fenn (40 minutes) and Kirkhope–Lerrick overnight (7 hours 30 minutes).

2. Check-in. Passengers travelling with a vehicle must check in at the terminal no later than 45 minutes before the scheduled departure time. Foot passengers must check in no later than 20 minutes before departure. Check-in closes at these times without exception, and passengers who arrive late will not be carried; their tickets will be treated as unused under the fare rules below. On the overnight Lerrick service, check-in for vehicles closes 60 minutes before departure.

3. Fare types. • Flexi fares can be amended free of charge up to 2 hours before departure, and are refundable in full, less a £10 administration fee, if cancelled at least 24 hours before departure. • Saver fares are non-refundable. They may be amended to another sailing on payment of a £25 amendment fee plus any fare difference, but only if the amendment is made at least 24 hours before the original departure. No amendments to Saver fares are possible within 24 hours of departure, and an unused Saver ticket has no value.

4. Vehicles. Vehicle fares are based on length and height. Vehicles over 1.85 m high, including vans and cars with roof boxes, pay the high-vehicle rate. Drivers must declare any gas cylinders and must switch off vehicle alarms before leaving the vehicle deck. Passengers may not remain on the vehicle deck during the crossing.

5. Pets. Dogs and cats may travel free of charge. On the Kirkhope–Stennar and Ardmore–Isle of Fenn routes, pets must remain in the owner's vehicle or, for foot passengers, in the designated outside deck area on a lead or in a carrier. Only on the overnight Kirkhope–Lerrick route is a pet-friendly lounge provided, and pet-friendly cabins may be booked on that route. Assistance dogs may accompany their owners in all passenger areas on all routes.

6. Luggage. Foot passengers may take up to two items of luggage of up to 20 kg each, plus one item of hand luggage, free of charge. Bicycles travel free on all routes but must be loaded by the passenger at the direction of the crew.

7. Cabins. Cabins on the overnight service are available from 21:30 and must be vacated 30 minutes before arrival. Cabin bookings are non-refundable within 7 days of departure.

8. Disruption. Where a sailing is cancelled for weather or technical reasons, passengers may travel on the next available sailing at no extra cost or receive a full refund, whatever the fare type. Northsound is not responsible for onward connections, accommodation or other consequential costs, except where required by law.

9. Concessions. Island residents holding a Northsound Resident Card receive 40% off standard passenger and car fares on routes serving their island.

10. Conduct. The Master may refuse to carry any passenger who is intoxicated or who behaves in a way likely to endanger the ship or other passengers.

LOAN AGREEMENT — INCOMING LOAN FOR EXHIBITION Borrower: Thornbury Museum and Art Gallery ("the Borrower") Lender: Mrs Eleanor Pryce-Morgan ("the Lender") Exhibition: "Coast and Country: Welsh Painting 1880–1930", Thornbury Museum, 6 March – 27 September 2027

Objects lent: (1) Gwilym Rees, "Harbour at Aberporth", oil on canvas, 1904. Agreed value £60,000. (2) Mary Lloyd Evans, "Study of Cliffs", watercolour on paper, 1911. Agreed value £15,000. (3) Mary Lloyd Evans, "Gorse in Bloom", watercolour on paper, 1912. Agreed value £10,000.

1. Loan period. The loan period runs from collection from the Lender's premises, planned for 15 February 2027, until return to the Lender's premises, planned for no later than 15 October 2027.

2. Insurance. The Borrower shall insure the objects at the agreed values, on a nail-to-nail basis covering all risks of physical loss or damage from the moment of removal from the Lender's wall until return to it, including transit and display. The Borrower shall bear the full cost of insurance and shall provide the Lender with a certificate of insurance before collection. The Lender's own household insurance shall not be relied upon.

3. Transport and couriers. The Borrower shall arrange and pay for packing and transport by a specialist fine-art carrier. The Lender may nominate a courier to accompany the objects on both journeys; the Borrower shall pay the courier's reasonable travel and subsistence costs.

4. Display conditions. Relative humidity shall be maintained at 45–55% and temperature at 18–22 °C. The two watercolours (objects 2 and 3) shall be displayed at a light level not exceeding 50 lux and shall not be exposed to direct daylight. The oil painting (object 1) may be displayed at up to 200 lux. All objects shall be displayed behind glazing or at a distance of at least 1 metre from visitors.

5. Condition and conservation. A condition report will be completed at collection, on installation and on return. The Borrower shall not undertake any conservation treatment, including surface cleaning, reframing or re-glazing, without the Lender's prior written consent. Any damage, however minor, must be reported to the Lender within 48 hours of discovery.

6. Photography and reproduction. The Borrower may photograph the objects for condition records, for the exhibition catalogue, and for publicity for the exhibition. Images may not be used on merchandise or licensed to third parties without the Lender's written agreement.

7. Credit line. The objects shall be credited "Lent by a private collector" on labels and in the catalogue. The Lender's name shall not be published.

8. Withdrawal. The Lender may withdraw any object at 30 days' notice if the Borrower breaches this agreement.

9. Costs. Except where stated otherwise, all costs arising from the loan shall be borne by the Borrower.

10. Governing law. This agreement is governed by the law of England and Wales.

1. Reporting repairs. Repairs can be reported 24 hours a day by telephone (0345 600 2210), online through My Account, or by email. Emergency repairs must be reported by telephone.

A follow-on repair may be needed. • Urgent: problems that seriously affect comfort or convenience, such as a blocked toilet where there is no other toilet, or loss of heating between 1 October and 30 April. We will complete the repair within 3 working days. • Routine: all other repairs, such as dripping taps, sticking doors or loose floor tiles. CALDERWOOD HOUSING GROUP — SICKNESS ABSENCE POLICY AND PROCEDURE (HR-12, revised 1 June 2026)

1. Scope. This policy applies to all employees. It does not apply to agency workers, whose absence is managed by their agency.

2. Reporting absence. If you are unable to attend work because of illness or injury, you must telephone your line manager personally by 09:30 on the first day of absence, or within one hour of your normal start time if you work shifts. Text messages, emails and messages passed on by colleagues are not acceptable except in exceptional circumstances. You must keep your manager updated at agreed intervals.

3. Certification. For absences of up to seven calendar days, you must complete a self-certification form on the HR portal on your return. For absences of eight calendar days or more, you must provide a fit note from a doctor or other authorised healthcare professional covering the eighth day onwards.

4. Sick pay. Employees who have completed their six-month probationary period are entitled to company sick pay of full basic pay for up to four weeks, followed by half basic pay for up to four further weeks, in any rolling 12-month period. Employees who have not yet completed probation are not entitled to company sick pay and will receive Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) only, if eligible. Company sick pay includes any SSP due.

5. Return-to-work meetings. Your line manager will hold a return-to-work meeting with you after every period of absence, normally on your first day back, to check you are fit to work and discuss any support you need.

6. Occupational health. Referrals to the Occupational Health (OH) service are made by the HR Advisory team, not by line managers, so that consent and medical confidentiality can be managed properly. HR will normally make a referral after four weeks' continuous absence, or after three separate absences within six months, or earlier at the request of the employee or line manager. You will be asked to consent to the release of the OH report to HR and your manager.

7. Trigger points. A formal Stage 1 attendance review will be held if an employee has three or more separate absences, or eight or more working days of absence, in any rolling 12-month period. Absences related to a disability may be discounted or the triggers adjusted as a reasonable adjustment, following OH advice.

8. Sickness during annual leave. If you fall ill during a period of booked annual leave, you may reclaim the leave days affected and treat them as sickness absence only if you (a) telephone your line manager on the first day of the illness, even if you are abroad, and (b) provide a fit note or, if abroad, a local medical certificate covering the days you were ill. Leave days cannot be reclaimed retrospectively without both of these.

9. Medical appointments. Employees should arrange medical and dental appointments outside working hours where possible. Reasonable paid time off is allowed for hospital appointments and for appointments related to pregnancy.

10. Keeping in touch. During long-term absence, your line manager will agree a means and frequency of contact with you. Contact is intended to support you and keep you informed, not to pressure you to return.

11. Fraudulent claims. Falsely claiming to be sick, or working elsewhere while on sick leave without permission, will be dealt with under the Disciplinary Policy and may be treated as gross misconduct.

1. Hours of control. Zone K operates Monday to Saturday, 08:30 to 18:30, including bank holidays except Christmas Day. Outside these hours, anyone may park in the resident bays without a permit.

2. Who can apply. A resident permit may be issued to a person whose main residence is within Zone K and who is the registered keeper of the vehicle at that address. Company cars are eligible only if the applicant provides a letter from their employer, on company letterhead, confirming that the vehicle is provided for their sole private use. Lease and hire-purchase vehicles are eligible with a copy of the agreement. Commercial vehicles over 3.5 tonnes are not eligible.

3. Resident permit charges (per year). • First vehicle in the household: £95. • Second vehicle: £160. • Third and subsequent vehicles: not available. • Fully electric vehicles (battery-electric, zero tailpipe emissions): the first permit in the household is free; a second permit is £80. Plug-in hybrid and other hybrid vehicles are not included in this discount and pay the standard charges. Permits are virtual and linked to the vehicle registration.

4. Visitor permits. Households may buy visitor permits in books of 20 half-day permits for £12 per book, up to a maximum of 120 half-day permits per household per year. Households where a resident is aged 70 or over receive an additional 60 half-day permits a year free of charge. The resident must activate each permit online or by scratching the date and time before the visitor parks.

5. Liability for penalty charges. A visitor permit authorises parking but does not transfer liability. Any Penalty Charge Notice (PCN) issued to a visitor's vehicle is the responsibility of the registered keeper of that vehicle, not of the resident who supplied the permit. Residents should ensure visitors understand where and when they may park.

6. Penalty charges. The PCN for parking in a resident bay without a valid permit is £70, reduced to £35 if paid within 14 days of issue. Representations against a PCN can be made online by the registered keeper.

7. Blue Badge holders. Blue Badge holders may park in resident bays without a permit for up to three hours, provided the badge and clock are displayed.

8. Refunds. Resident permits may be surrendered at any time for a refund for each complete remaining month, less a £10 administration fee. Visitor permits are non-refundable.

9. Applications. Applications are processed by Northam Parking Services within 10 working days. Permits are valid from the date shown on the confirmation email.

10. Trades. Tradespeople working at a property in Zone K can buy a trade permit at £8 per day.

FERNHILL FOODS LIMITED — MINUTES OF A MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS Held at the registered office, Unit 4, Wharfside Park, Grimsby, on Thursday 19 November 2026 at 10:00.

Present: Mrs K. Adeyemi (Chair, non-executive), Mr P. Lindqvist (Chief Executive), Ms R. Banerjee (Chief Financial Officer), Mr T. Hollis (Operations Director), Mrs J. Carver (non-executive). In attendance: Mr O. Reid (Company Secretary).

1. Quorum and conflicts. The Chair confirmed that a quorum was present. Mr Hollis declared an interest in item 5, as his brother-in-law is a director of Arden Packaging Ltd, and did not take part in that decision.

2. Minutes. The minutes of the meeting held on 17 September 2026 were approved and signed by the Chair.

3. Trading update. The CFO reported revenue for the seven months to 31 October of £18.4 million, 6% ahead of the same period last year, and EBITDA of £1.9 million, 4% behind budget, mainly due to higher energy and fish costs. Net debt stood at £5.2 million.

4. Interim dividend. The Board declared an interim dividend of 3.5 pence per ordinary share, to be paid on 15 January 2027 to shareholders on the register at the close of business on 11 December 2026. The CFO confirmed that distributable reserves were sufficient.

5. Capital expenditure. The Board approved capital expenditure of up to £1.2 million for a new automated packing line at the Grimsby site, conditional on the bank confirming the extension of the asset finance facility. Arden Packaging Ltd was selected as preferred supplier. The Operations Director will not be involved in contract negotiations, which will be led by the Chief Executive.

6. Pricing. Following discussion of input costs and customer relationships, the Board resolved that list prices to retail customers will not be increased before 1 April 2027. The Commercial team will prepare a proposal for a price review, to be considered at the February 2027 meeting.

7. Remuneration. The Board noted that 2026 bonuses for executive directors and the senior leadership team will be determined by the Remuneration Committee, chaired by Mrs Carver, at its meeting in January 2027. The Chief Executive will provide performance information for the senior leadership team but will not determine any awards. Executive directors will not take part in decisions on their own remuneration.

8. Recruitment. The Board approved a freeze on recruitment to new non-production posts until 31 March 2027. Replacement hires and production roles are exempt.

9. Budget 2027–28. The CFO will present a draft budget for 2027–28 at the February 2027 meeting.

10. Any other business. The Chair noted that the annual food-safety audit had been passed with an AA grade.

11. Next meeting. Thursday 18 February 2027 at 10:00.

The meeting closed at 12:40.

ROWAN TREE DENTAL PRACTICE — PATIENT INFORMATION AND PRACTICE POLICIES (updated September 2026)

1. NHS and private care. We provide both NHS and private dental treatment. Your dentist will explain which treatments are available on the NHS and which are private, and will give you a written treatment plan with costs before any course of treatment begins.

2. NHS charges (England, from April 2026). Band 1 (examination, diagnosis, X-rays, scale and polish if clinically needed): £27.40. Band 2 (Band 1 plus fillings, root canal treatment, extractions): £75.30. Band 3 (Band 2 plus crowns, dentures, bridges): £326.70. Urgent treatment: £27.40. NHS charges for a course of treatment are payable in full at your first appointment of that course, before treatment starts. If the band changes during the course, any difference is payable at the next appointment.

3. Who gets free NHS treatment. NHS dental treatment is free for children under 18, and for 18-year-olds only if they are in qualifying full-time education. It is also free for those who are pregnant or have had a baby in the last 12 months, NHS inpatients treated by the hospital dentist, and people receiving certain benefits or holding a valid HC2 certificate. You will be asked to show evidence of exemption; we check claims, and penalty charges may be issued by the NHS for incorrect claims.

4. Private fees. Private examinations cost £55 and hygienist appointments £68. Private treatment is paid for on the day of each appointment.

5. Missed and late-cancelled appointments. For private appointments, a charge of £40 is made if you fail to attend or cancel with less than 24 hours' notice. This charge does not apply to NHS appointments, as NHS regulations do not allow it; however, NHS patients who miss two appointments without notice within 12 months may be asked to find another practice for future routine care.

6. Emergency appointments. Same-day emergency appointments are released at 08:00 each weekday and are offered by telephone (01632 960 418) on a first-come, first-served basis. Outside opening hours, call NHS 111.

7. Children. Children under 16 must be accompanied by a parent, guardian or adult with parental responsibility at every appointment.

8. Medical history. Please update your medical history form at every check-up, including any new medicines, as some affect dental treatment.

9. Recall intervals. Your dentist will recommend how often you need a check-up, between 3 and 24 months for adults and 3 and 12 months for children, based on your oral health.

10. Feedback and complaints. Please speak to the Practice Manager, Mrs D. Kaur, in the first instance. If you remain unhappy, you can contact NHS England or, for private treatment, the Dental Complaints Service.

11. Opening hours. Monday to Friday 08:00–17:30; Wednesday late surgery until 19:30.
